Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

live verb

be alive

also be alive, alive, living, live on, as long as I live, on my life!, as I live!, as sure as I live

classical

Ter. Haut. 429: valet atque vīvit
Cic. Sen. 24: annum … posse vīvere

vīvō, vīvere, vīxī, vīctum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

live, be alive

What one lives on goes in the ablative: lacte atque pecore vīvunt (Caes. BG 4.1.8). Dum vīvō, as long as I live; ita vīvam!, as I live! (Cic. Fam. 2.13.3, Lewis & Short; Traupman 102).

Other words

  • vīvus, vīva, vīvum — alive, living

    also used · classical · Phaedr. 3.16.19: sīc vīva quod negārat tribuit mortua; Traupman 341 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • Ita vīvam! — on my life! as I live!

    subjunctive of wish, “so may I live”, as an oath · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.13.3: nam, ita vīvam, putāvī (Lewis & Short), s.v. vīvō; Cic. Fam. 16.20.1: sollicitat, ita vīvam, mē tua valētūdō (Lewis & Short), s.v. ita; Traupman 102

Examples

  • līberī quid agunt meī, quōs relīquī hīc, fīlium atque fīliam? — Vīvont, valent.

    How are my children, whom I left here, my son and my daughter? — Alive and well.Plaut. Trin. 1074–1075

  • nēmō enim est tam senex quī sē annum nōn putet posse vīvere

    for no one is so old that he does not think he can live another yearCic. Sen. 24

  • neque multum frūmentō, sed maximam partem lacte atque pecore vīvunt

    they live not much on grain, but mostly on milk and the meat of their herdsCaes. BG 4.1.8

See also live, life, die, be born.
